plan: Genesis 11:1-9, 10-26; 1 Chronicles 1:24-27; Genesis 11:27-31; Genesis 12:1-9, 10-20; Genesis 13:1-18; Genesis 14:1-16, 17-24

readings.title: The Rebellion at Shinar
readings.subtitle: Engineering an Independent City
readings.text: [Genesis 11:1] And all the earth had one language and one speech. [2] And it came to be, as they set out from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinʽar, and they dwelt there. [3] And they said to each other, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” And they had brick for stone, and they had asphalt for mortar. [4] And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top is in the heavens, and make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over all the face of the earth.”

readings.title: YeHoVaH Intervenes at Babel
readings.subtitle: The Origin of Root Languages
readings.text: [5] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down to see <dn>את</dn> the city and <dn>את</dn> the tower which the sons of men had built. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Look, they are one people and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do! And now, they are not going to be withheld from doing whatever they plan to do.</dq> [7] <dq>“Come, let <dn>Us</dn> go there and confuse their language, so that they do not understand one another’s speech.”</dq> [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> scattered <dn>את</dn> them from there, over the face of all the earth, and they left off building the city. [9] That is why its name was called Baḇel, because there <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> confused the language of all the earth, and from there <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> scattered them over the face of all the earth.

readings.title: The Generations of Shem
readings.subtitle: Preserving the Patriarchal Line
readings.text: [Genesis 11:10] This is the genealogy of Shĕm: Shĕm was a hundred years old and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Arpaḵshaḏ, two years after the flood. [11] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Arpaḵshaḏ, Shĕm lived five hundred years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [12] And Arpaḵshaḏ lived thirty-five years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shelaḥ. [13] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Shelaḥ, Arpaḵshaḏ lived four hundred and three years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [14] And Shelaḥ lived thirty years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ěḇer. [15] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ěḇer, Shelaḥ lived four hundred and three years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [16] And Ěḇer lived thirty-four years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Peleḡ. [17] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Peleḡ, Ěḇer lived four hundred and thirty years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [18] And Peleḡ lived thirty years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Reʽu. [19] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Reʽu, Peleḡ lived two hundred and nine years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [20] And Reʽu lived thirty-two years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Seruḡ. [21] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Seruḡ, Reʽu lived two hundred and seven years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [22] And Seruḡ lived thirty years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Naḥor. [23] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Naḥor, Seruḡ lived two hundred years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [24] And Naḥor lived twenty-nine years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Teraḥ. [25] And after he brought forth <dn>את</dn> Teraḥ, Naḥor lived one hundred and nineteen years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [26] And Teraḥ lived seventy years, and brought forth <dn>את</dn> Aḇram, <dn>את</dn> Naḥor, and <dn>את</dn> Haran.

readings.title: The Ancestry of Avraham
readings.subtitle: The Chronicle of Shem's Descendants
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:24] Shĕm, Arpaḵshaḏ, Shĕlah, [25] Ěḇer, Peleḡ, Reʽu, [26] Seruḡ, Naḥor, Teraḥ, [27] and Aḇram, that is Aḇraham.

readings.title: The Origins of Abram
readings.subtitle: Departure from the Ur of the Chaldeans
readings.text: [Genesis 11:27] And this is the genealogy of Teraḥ: Teraḥ brought forth <dn>את</dn> Aḇram, <dn>את</dn> Naḥor, and <dn>את</dn> Haran. And Haran brought forth <dn>את</dn> Lot. [28] And Haran died before his father Teraḥ in the land of his birth, in Ur-kasdim. [29] And Aḇram and Naḥor took wives: the name of Aḇram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Naḥor’s wife, Milkah, the daughter of Haran the father of Milkah and the father of Yiskah. [30] And Sarai was barren, she had no child. [31] And Teraḥ took <dn>את</dn> his son Aḇram and <dn>את</dn> his grandson Lot, son of Haran, and <dn>את</dn> his daughter-in-law Sarai, his son Aḇram’s wife, and they went out with <dn>את</dn> them from Ur-kasdim to go to the land of Kenaʽan. And they came to Ḥaran and dwelt there. [32] And the days of Teraḥ came to be two hundred and five years, and Teraḥ died in Aran.

readings.title: The Call of Abram
readings.subtitle: Promises of the Birthright
readings.text: [Genesis 12:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Aḇram, <dq>“Go yourself out of your land, from your relatives and from your father’s house, to a land which <dn>I</dn> show you.</dq> [2] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make you a great nation, and bless you and make your name great, and you shall be a blessing!</dq> [3] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bless those who bless you, and curse him who curses you. And in you all the clans of the earth shall be blessed.”</dq> [4] So Aḇram left, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded him, and Lot went with <dn>את</dn> him. And Aḇram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Ḥaran.

readings.title: Arrival in Kenaʽan
readings.subtitle: Establishing Sites of Worship
readings.text: [5] And Aḇram took <dn>את</dn> Sarai his wife and <dn>את</dn> Lot his brother’s son, and <dn>את</dn> all their possessions that they had gathered, and <dn>את</dn> the beings whom they had acquired in Ḥaran, and they set out for the land of Kenaʽan. And they came to the land of Kenaʽan. [6] And Aḇram passed through the land to the place of Sheḵem, as far as the terebinth tree of Moreh. At that time the Kenaʽanites were in the land. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Aḇram and said, <dq>“To your seed <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> this land.”</dq> And he built there a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who had appeared to him. [8] And from there he moved to the mountain east of Bĕyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, and he pitched his tent, with Bĕyth <dn>Ěl</dn> on the west and Ai on the east. And he built there a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and called on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [9] And Aḇram set out, continuing toward the South.

readings.title: Abram Seeks Refuge
readings.subtitle: A Plan of Deception
readings.text: [Genesis 12:10] And a scarcity of food came to be in the land, and Aḇram went down to Mitsrayim to dwell there, for the scarcity of food was severe in the land. [11] And it came to be, when he was close to entering Mitsrayim, that he said to Sarai his wife, “See, I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at. [12] “And it shall be, when the Mitsrites see <dn>את</dn> you, that they shall say, ‘This is his wife.’ And they shall kill <dn>את</dn> me, but let you live. [13] “Please say you are my sister, so that it shall be well with me for your sake, and my life be spared because of you.”

readings.title: Plagues Upon Pharaoh
readings.subtitle: The Preservation of Sarai
readings.text: [14] And it came to be, when Aḇram came into Mitsrayim, that the Mitsrites saw <dn>את</dn> the woman, that she was very beautiful. [15] And Pharaoh’s officials saw <dn>את</dn> her and praised <dn>את</dn> her before Pharaoh, and the woman was taken to Pharaoh’s house. [16] And he treated Aḇram well for her sake, and he had sheep, and cattle, and male donkeys, and male and female servants, and female donkeys, and camels. [17] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> plagued <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh and <dn>את</dn> his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Aḇram’s wife. [18] And Pharaoh called Aḇram and said, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not inform me that she was your wife? [19] “Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’? And so I was going to take <dn>את</dn> her for my wife. Look, here is your wife, take her and go.” [20] And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him, and they sent <dn>את</dn> him away, with <dn>את</dn> his wife and <dn>את</dn> all that he had.

readings.title: Return to the South
readings.subtitle: Strife Among the Herdsmen
readings.text: [Genesis 13:1] And Aḇram went up from Mitsrayim into the South, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him. [2] And Aḇram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold. [3] And he went on his journey from the South as far as Bĕyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bĕyth <dn>Ěl</dn> and Ai, [4] to the place of the slaughter-place which he had made there at first. And there Aḇram called on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [5] Now Lot, who went with <dn>את</dn> Aḇram, also had flocks and herds and tents. [6] And the land was not able to bear <dn>את</dn> them, that they might dwell together, for their possessions were great, so that they could not dwell together. [7] And there was strife between the herdsmen of Aḇram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. And at that time the Kenaʽanites and the Perizzites dwelt in the land.

readings.title: Parting Ways
readings.subtitle: Pitching Tents Toward Sedom
readings.text: [8] Then Aḇram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between you and me, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers. [9] “Is not all the land before you? Please separate from me. If you take the left, then I go to the right; or, if you go to the right, then I go to the left.” [10] And Lot lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> all the plain of the Yardĕn, that it was well watered everywhere – before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> Seḏom and <dn>את</dn> Amorah – like the garden of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, like the land of Mitsrayim as you go toward Tsoʽar. [11] So Lot chose for himself <dn>את</dn> all the plain of the Yardĕn, and Lot moved east. Thus they separated from each other, [12] Aḇram dwelling in the land of Kenaʽan, and Lot dwelling in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent as far as Seḏom. [13] But the men of Seḏom were evil and sinned before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, exceedingly so.

readings.title: The Promise Renewed
readings.subtitle: Walking the Breadth of the Land
readings.text: [14] And after Lot had separated from him, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Aḇram, <dq>“Now lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,</dq> [15] <dq>for <dn>את</dn> all the land which you see <dn>I</dn> shall give to you and your seed forever.</dq> [16] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> your seed as the dust of the earth, so that, if a man could count <dn>את</dn> the dust of the earth, then your seed also could be counted.</dq> [17] <dq>“Arise, walk in the land through its length and its width, for <dn>I</dn> give it to you.”</dq> [18] So Aḇram moved his tent, and went and dwelt by the terebinth trees of Mamrĕ, which are in Ḥeḇron, and built a slaughter-place there to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Rebellion of the Kings
readings.subtitle: Lot Taken Captive
readings.text: [Genesis 14:1] And it came to be in the days of Amraphel sovereign of Shinʽar, Aryoḵ sovereign of Ellasar, Keḏorlaʽomer sovereign of Ěylam, and Tiḏʽal sovereign of Goyim, [2] that they fought against Bera sovereign of Seḏom, Birsha sovereign of Amorah, Shinaḇ sovereign of Aḏmah, Shem’ĕḇer sovereign of Tseḇoyim, and the sovereign of Bela, that is Tsoʽar. [3] All these joined together in the Valley of Siddim, that is the Salt Sea. [4] Twelve years they served <dn>את</dn> Keḏorlaʽomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled. [5] And in the fourteenth year Keḏorlaʽomer and the sovereigns that were with <dn>את</dn> him came and struck <dn>את</dn> the Repha’im in Ashteroth Qarnayim, and <dn>את</dn> the Zuzim in Ḥam, and <dn>את</dn> the Ěmites in Shavĕh Qiryathayim, [6] and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥorites in their mountain of Sĕʽir, as far as <dn>Ěl</dn> Paran, which is by the wilderness. [7] And they turned back and came to Ěn Mishpat, that is Qaḏĕsh, and struck <dn>את</dn> all the country of the Amalĕqites, and also <dn>את</dn> the Amorites who dwelt in Ḥatsetson Tamar. [8] And the sovereign of Seḏom, and the sovereign of Amorah, and the sovereign of Aḏmah, and the sovereign of Tseḇoyim, and the sovereign of Bela, that is Tsoʽar, went out and joined together in battle in the Valley of Siddim, [9] against Keḏorlaʽomer sovereign of Ěylam, and Tiḏʽal sovereign of Goyim, and Amraphel sovereign of Shinʽar, and Aryoḵ sovereign of Ellasar – four sovereigns against five. [10] And the Valley of Siddim had many tar pits. And the sovereigns of Seḏom and Amorah fled and fell there, and the remainder fled to the mountains. [11] And they took <dn>את</dn> all the goods of Seḏom and Amorah, and <dn>את</dn> all their food, and went away. [12] And they took <dn>את</dn> Lot, Aḇram’s brother’s son who dwelt in Seḏom, and <dn>את</dn> his goods, and left.

readings.title: Abram the Hebrew Strikes
readings.subtitle: The Rescue of the Captives
readings.text: [13] And one who had escaped came and informed Aḇram the Hebrew, for he dwelt by the terebinth trees of Mamrĕ the Amorite, brother of Eshkol and brother of Anĕr, and they had a covenant with Aḇram. [14] And when Aḇram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed <dn>את</dn> his three hundred and eighteen trained servants who were born in his own house, and went in pursuit as far as Dan. [15] And he and his servants divided against them by night, and struck them and pursued them as far as Ḥoḇah, which is on the left of Dammeseq. [16] So he brought back <dn>את</dn> all the goods, and also brought back <dn>את</dn> his brother Lot and <dn>את</dn> his goods, as well as <dn>את</dn> the women and <dn>את</dn> the people.

readings.section: The Priesthood of the Most High
readings.title: Malkitsedeq Blesses Abram
readings.subtitle: The Tithe to El Elyon
readings.text: [Genesis 14:17] And after his return from the striking of <dn>את</dn> Keḏorlaʽomer and <dn>את</dn> the sovereigns who were with <dn>את</dn> him, the sovereign of Seḏom came out to meet him at the Valley of Shavĕh, that is, the Sovereign’s Valley. [18] And Malkitseḏeq sovereign of Shalĕm brought out bread and wine. Now he was the priest of the Most High <dn>Ěl</dn>. [19] And he blessed him and said, “Blessed be Aḇram of the Most High <dn>Ěl</dn>, Possessor of the heavens and earth. [20] “And blessed be the Most High <dn>Ěl</dn> who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” And he gave him a tenth of all.

readings.title: A Hand Lifted to the Possessor
readings.subtitle: Rejecting Compromised Wealth
readings.text: [21] And the sovereign of Seḏom said to Aḇram, “Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.” [22] But Aḇram said to the sovereign of Seḏom, “I have lifted my hand to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Most High <dn>Ěl</dn>, the Possessor of the heavens and earth, [23] not to take a thread or a sandal strap or whatever is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made <dn>את</dn> Aḇram rich,’ [24] except only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with <dn>את</dn> me: Anĕr, Eshkol, and Mamrĕ. Let them take their portion.”
